Howev- er, adverse effects such as sedation and hypotension may limit use. 1. Ahmed I, Takeshita J. Clonidine: a critical review of its role in the treatment of psychiatric disorders. CNS Drugs 1996; 6: 53–70. Growth retardation. Clonidine has been reported to be a stimulant of growth hormone release, presumably as a result of central alpha-adrenergic stimulation, and has been tried in the di- agnosis and management of growth retardation (p.1798). It may be given orally as a provocative test for growth hormone defi- ciency,1,2 particularly in children,3 although some consider meas- urement of circulating somatomedins (insulin-like growth fac- tors; IGFs) to be more useful than provocative tests.
